title: a block decoder wrote a full 8x8 block regardless of how much of it lay inside the tile
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a fixed-size block write at the edge of a region that is not a multiple of the block
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct av_malloc-family allocation, no inner layer. FFmpeg's av_malloc is malloc plus alignment.
fidelity: model consumer, real arithmetic: the sizes and the crossing expression are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md.
live_proof: absent at the pin: n9.0.1:libavcodec/exr.c carries `int bw = FFMIN(8, td->xsize - x);` and `int bh = FFMIN(8, td->ysize - y);` with the loops bounded by them. The unclamped `yy < 8` / `xx < 8` form is at f45da79b2c33^ and is absent from the pin. A fix-reversal.

The request is exactly a jemalloc size class, so the usable size equals the requested size and there is no slack to absorb the crossing -- confirmed by tools/size-class-audit.py, which reports `faults` for this case. The capability's bounds end where the allocation does and the probe SHOULD fault.

ASan reports heap-buffer-overflow at the labelled probe on the buggy arm and is silent on the fixed arm -- keyed on heap-buffer-overflow, never on the string AddressSanitizer.

status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from av_malloc / av_mallocz / av_calloc / av_malloc_array -- which on the platform is malloc -- with no AVBufferPool or AVRefStructPool between it and the request. So under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the loop steps in 8s and the BLOCK is always written whole, so the crossing appears only when the tile's dimensions are not multiples of 8 -- a property of the image rather than of any index. That is why the fix clamps with FFMIN against the tile's own xsize and ysize rather than bounding the destination.
